newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia says to attend meeting of ex-Yugo bankers.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia says to attend meeting of ex-Yugo bankers.

text.p: The Bank of Slovenia said on Monday governor France Arhar would attend a meeting of central bank governors of the former Yugoslav republics in the town of Ohrid in Macedonia on September 16.
The bank said the governors planned to discuss a proposal by the Bank for International Settlements for the division of ex-Yugoslav assets.

Central bank governors of Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Macedonia held their first meeting since the break-up of the former federation in Bled in Slovenia on July 25, when they said they in principle supported the BIS proposal.

The Basle-based BIS has suggested the assets of the former Yugoslavia, valued at around $660 million, should be divided according to a plan introduced by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), which would give Slovenia a 16.39 percent stake.
Croatia would get 28.49 percent, Bosnia 13.2, Macedonia 5.4 and rump Yugoslavia 36.52 percent of the assets.
The bulk of the former federation's assets comprise gold reserves, valued at about $600 million, which have been held by the BIS since before the break-up of Yugoslavia in 1991.

The Bank of Slovenia said earlier the Belgrade-based National Bank of Yugoslavia would be invited to the September meeting although it did not attend the first meeting in Bled, claiming it was not authorised to discuss the division of pre-1991 assets.
Sharing out those assets is seen as a key condition for individual repulibcs to settle their respective shares of the former Yugoslavia's outstanding commercial debt of about $4.3 billion.

Slovenia was the first republic to reach an accord with its creditors, shouldering 18 percent of the debt and completing the deal in spite of legal challenge by rump Yugoslavia. Croatia concluded a similar agreement, taking on 29.5 percent of the debt. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
